messages:
jenna-customer: hey support — we rotated the API key in Vault for the payments service ~10:00 UTC and within a few minutes background jobs started getting 401s. Web UI requests look fine for some tenants, but others fail. Also seeing a billing spike from retries. any ideas?

matt-support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a failing request ID and a short curl that reproduces? also did you do a revoke or a staged rotation?

jenna-customer: here are a couple of logs and a curl we used to reproduce:
```
# log from job worker
ERROR auth: token validation failed tenant=acme request_id=rcpt-9a8b status=401 signature_mismatch
# curl repro
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotated-key>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/payments/status
```
we rotated via our vault pipeline which ran `vault kv put secret/payments api_key=... revoke=true` — I think we used the revoke flag because we wanted immediate cutover.

sophia-devex: thanks, two quick hypotheses: 1) the key in Vault was rewrapped with a different KMS key id (kid) so tokens signed under the old kid no longer validate, and 2) long-lived sidecars / background workers still have the old key in memory and couldn't refresh because revoke was immediate. can you confirm whether you changed the KMS alias during the rotation?

vault-bot: [vault] kv-v2 write secret/payments by user=jenna-ci pipeline=rotate-2026-03-17 revoke=true rewrap_kms_key_alias=projects/prod-kms/locations/global/keyRolloverAlias

oncall-ops: looking at the cluster: the k8s secret `payments-api-key` was updated in the kube-apiserver, but the deployment `payments-worker` has not restarted — sidecar env-injector doesn't force a restart on secret change for that annotation. `kubectl get pods -l app=payments-worker` shows pods still on old env.

oncall-ops: run this to force a restart (recommended quick fix):
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/payments-worker -n billing
# then verify the env var value inside a restarted pod
kubectl exec -it $(kubectl get pod -l app=payments-worker -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -n billing -- env | grep PAYMENT_API_KEY
```

matt-support: also check Vault audit for read errors from the sidecar; if revoke happened immediately the injector might be failing to unwrap the wrapped key (403) and falling back to cached token which is now invalid. that would explain per-tenant variability if some jobs hit new pods and some hit old ones.

jenna-customer: rolled the workers ~3m ago with `kubectl rollout restart` — failures dropped to zero and billing retries normalized. thanks.

sophia-devex: great. root-cause notes for internal follow-up: immediate `revoke=true` combined with a KMS rewrap (alias rotated) caused token/signature mismatch for clients that had not reloaded env; sidecars failing to unwrap against the new KMS key returned errors and left processes with stale cached keys, causing 401s and retry storms.

matt-support: next steps / mitigation we recommend to the customer: 1) avoid immediate revoke when changing KMS alias; use staged rotation + grace window so processes can renew before old key invalidates, 2) add a post-rotate hook to `kubectl rollout restart` critical worker deployments or use lifecycle hooks that force env reload, 3) add a Vault read failure alert for unwrap/403s, 4) throttle retries in the job runner to avoid billing spikes.

jenna-customer: appreciated — we'll add a staged workflow in our pipeline and implement a restart hook. please open an internal ticket so we can sync on adding a console doc for `rotation-grace-window` guidance. :+1:

matt-support: filed INT-rotations-1123 to track changes to docs and a preflight check in `redwood-cli` to detect KMS alias changes during rotation. we'll follow up with a short postmortem template.

jenna-customer: thanks everyone, incident resolved from our side."
